audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases — Dr. Mundo RESISTS the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, taking health loss and dropping a cannister instead — appears nowhere in either layer. Not one field mentions it.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction of the matchup and nothing else comes close. Nautilus's entire kit is immobilising CC: Staggering Blow's root, Dredge Line's pull, Depth Charge's knock-up and stun. Against Mundo the first one is simply deleted. A player who does not know this will open with Depth Charge, watch it evaporate, and lose a 120-second cooldown for nothing. The correct sequence — spend the cheap root first to pop the passive, then land the real CC — was never written down.
audit.corrected: The passive is now stated in dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[2] area, whys[4], spikes[1].text, mid, late, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[0], with the sequencing rule attached each time.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields (early, mid, whys[2], wants.foe[0]) credit Infected Bonesaw with a self-heal and with costing Mundo health. Riot's Q text says only: damage based on the target's CURRENT health, plus a slow, at 0 cost. The healing lives on Heart Zapper (W) and Maximum Dosage (R). Heart Zapper's own rule was also never stated: it stores a portion of damage he takes and heals him only IF its end-of-duration burst hits an enemy.
audit.why: Mundo has not paid health for his Q in years, so 'his poke costs him HP' teaches a player to trade into it. And the Heart Zapper rule is free counterplay that was sitting unused: step outside its 325 radius before the burst lands and he heals nothing at all.
audit.corrected: Q restated as current-health scaling with a 975-range slow and no heal; Heart Zapper's 17s cooldown, 325 radius and burst-must-connect rule written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and dontsFull[0].d.
sources: enemyKit Q text, cost 0, range 975, cd 4

audit.whatIsWrong: Maximum Dosage was named in six fields with no cooldown, and Heart Zapper — the matchup's tracked ability — likewise had none.
audit.why: Maximum Dosage is a flat 120 seconds at every rank, the same as Depth Charge at rank 1, which is exactly the trade a player needs to reason about. Heart Zapper's 17s is the short window everything else fits inside.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written in across the cooldown fields, mid, late and wants.foe[2].

audit.why: Both layers already carry the same chart (Nautilus, Nautilus, Skill, Skill, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo), it agrees row-for-row with the whys, and the mirror audit explicitly left it alone because the packet's own chart for this matchup is flagged defective. No chart edits proposed.

edits.after: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: 17s at rank 1 — it only heals him if the burst catches someone, so step outside its 325 radius before it pops. - Maximum Dosage: a flat 120s. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are your only clean window. Mundo is one of the weakest early laners in the game - his Cleaver poke costs him HP via the passive heal mechanic and he can't trade back when you land Q. Hit your level 2-3 spike (Q + W + E online) and punish: Q-pull into your passive root, weave E slows and W splash burn, and force him off the wave. Dodge his Cleaver - every one he lands is percent-HP poke plus a self-heal, so sidestepping it doubles as denying his sustain.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are your only clean window. Mundo is one of the weakest early laners in the game - Infected Bonesaw scales off your current health so it stings least once you are chunked, and he can't trade back when you land Q. Hit your level 2-3 spike (Q + W + E online) and punish: Q-pull into your passive root, weave E slows and W splash burn, and force him off the wave. Dodge the bonesaw - each one is free poke plus a 975-range slow that keeps you outside hook range.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 the lane slips. Your W shield and E still let you win a raw short trade, but Mundo's passive regen and Q self-heal mean he just walks back to lane and erases your poke. At 6 your Depth Charge looks like a kill - it isn't. He pops Maximum Dosage and heals through the entire knock-up-into-CC chain. Treat your ult as a gank-setup tool: your CC is undodgeable, so call your jungler and use the lockdown to get a kill you can't secure 1v1.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 the lane slips. Your W shield and E still let you win a raw short trade, but his passive regen and Heart Zapper's stored-damage heal mean he just walks back to lane and erases your poke. At 6 your Depth Charge looks like a kill - it isn't. His passive resists the first immobilise outright, then Maximum Dosage heals a chunk of his missing health on a flat 120s. Treat your ult as gank setup: spend the root first, call your jungler, and take the kill you can't secure 1v1.

edits.before: This is where you lose, and it's by design. Mundo scales forever - Heartsteel, tank items, and Maximum Dosage make him functionally unkillable inside your CC duration, while his Cleaver percent-HP poke and E bonus damage shred your tank stats that don't fight back. Your damage is flat and front-loaded; his is percent-HP and infinite. Accept you're now a CC-bot: land Depth Charge and Q to peel and lock him for your carries, because you will never out-duel a fed drain-tank.
edits.after: This is where you lose, and it's by design. Mundo scales forever - tank items and Maximum Dosage make him functionally unkillable inside your CC duration, and his passive resists the first immobilise before any of the chain even starts. Your damage is flat and front-loaded; his bonesaw scales off your current health and never stops coming. Accept you're now a CC-bot: land Depth Charge and Q to peel and lock him for your carries, because you will never out-duel a fed drain-tank.

notes: The largest gap in my whole slice: Dr. Mundo's passive resisting the FIRST immobilising effect was absent from every field of both layers, in a matchup where the champion's entire kit is immobilising CC. The correct play — spend Staggering Blow's root or Dredge Line to pop the passive, THEN commit Depth Charge — now appears in seven places. Second: Infected Bonesaw was credited with a self-heal and a health cost in four fields; Riot's text gives it neither (cost 0, current-health scaling, slow), and the healing belongs to Heart Zapper and Maximum Dosage. Heart Zapper's burst-must-connect rule is free counterplay that had never been written down.
